title: Peel open a sterile pouch with both hands and drop its forceps onto the sterile field without touching them
instruction: Open the sterile pouch and drop the forceps onto the sterile field without touching the forceps or the drape.
context: Opening sterile supplies onto a sterile field starts every minor-procedure and dental tray setup, and is routine for medical assistants (O*NET 31-9092, about 0.8 M US workers) and dental assistants (31-9091, about 0.37 M). The opener may touch only the outside of the pouch: one unsealed tab in each hand, the plies peeled apart over the field until the instrument drops out, with neither the hands nor the pouch touching the field. The pouch starts flat, so one hand must lift it by the top tab before the other can take the lower one. The seal parts only under a steady two-handed pull of about 3 N, and the pouch hangs free, so the peel must be symmetric, level and high enough that the pouch never brushes the drape, and long enough (about 21 cm) that the forceps falls inside the field's 2.5 cm non-sterile border.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the table top (x forward, y left). Pouch: 3.5 x 9 in (89 x 229 mm) self-seal paper/film sterilization pouch with a chevron seal (McKesson Argent Sure-Check 73-SSP381), holding 5.5 in (14 cm, 30 g) stainless dressing forceps. It lies flat, paper up, on a rest: a 24 cm length of 30 x 40 mm pine batten taped to the table, centred at x 24, from y 0.2 to 24.2. The pouch's length runs across the table, its chevron end toward the right arm at y 0, 2 mm past the batten's end. The 20 mm unsealed paper tab beyond the chevron is turned up; the film tab hangs down over the batten's end. Drape: blue sterile poly-lined towel drape, 18 x 26 in (Dynarex 4410), flat and taped, centred at x 52, y 0, long side across; near edge at x 29. Nothing else on the table; same layout every trial.
scoring: Latched for the whole trial: 0 if a gripper touches the forceps or the drape (sim: a pad tip or tool point within 8 mm of the forceps, or within 1 cm of the drape top over it; real: trial video). At the end: 1.0 the forceps lies directly on the drape, still, every point at least 2.5 cm in from the drape's edges, and the pouch never touched the drape, held 1 s (real: photo with a ruler; pouch contact from the video); 0.5 the same but part of the forceps within the 2.5 cm border; 0.25 forceps on the drape but the pouch touched the drape; 0.2 forceps not on the drape (in the pouch, in the air, on the pouch or the table) with the seal open along its whole length (real: photo of the separated plies); 0.1 seal open from the chevron at least half its length, 105 mm (ruler); otherwise 0. 'Directly on the drape': its lowest point within 1 mm of the drape's top in sim, so forceps lying on the pouch does not count.
reset_notes: One new pouch per trial: slide the forceps in tips first, close the self-seal flap (no sterilizer needed; the pouch is a training stand-in), lay it flat on the batten paper up, chevron end 2 mm past the batten's end, turn the paper tab up and let the film tab hang, by hand. Lay and tape a fresh or uncreased drape. About 1 minute.
fidelity: Approximate. Each ply is 11 hinged rigid strips plus a tab (1.5 mm colliders, 1.5 g each; the real sheet is 0.1 mm, 0.15 g). The plies are joined at 12 seal lines by two point joints each that break at 1.6 N (3.2 N per line), from the EN 868-5 minimum seal strength of 1.5 N per 15 mm. They break on load size, not direction. No tearing. Gripper contact is checked by distance from the pad tips and tool point, the real trial by video.
